question:
A 84-year-old man presents to the emergency department with active left-sided epistaxis. He says that
the episode started 2 hours ago and, when asked to estimate the amount of bleeding, he produces a
hand towel saturated with blood. He has a history of atrial fibrillation, hypertension,
hypercholesterolemia, mild chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and a mitral-valve replacement with
a bioprosthetic valve 5 years ago. His medications include metoprolol and apixaban. He is afebrile with
a heart rate of 110 beats per minute, a blood pressure of 122/83 mm Hg, and a respiratory rate of 15
breaths per minute. His oxygen saturation is 98% while he is breathing ambient air. Examination
reveals severe ongoing epistaxis from the left nares without a clearly identified source of bleeding;
there is also blood visible in the posterior oropharynx. In addition to fluid resuscitation, which one of the
following management strategies should be undertaken next in this case? Answer Choices: (A)
Perform an endonasal examination, and apply topical silver nitrate (B) Administer andexanet alfa (C)
Consult interventional radiology for embolization of the bleeding vessel (D) Reverse anticoagulation
with fresh frozen plasma (E) Place an anterior nasal pack (F) Observe the patient for spontaneous
resolution of bleeding (G) Place an anterior and a posterior nasal pack (H) Perform surgical ligation of
the sphenopalatine artery (I) Perform nasal endoscopy and cauterize the bleeding vessel (J)
Administer tranexamic acid intranasally
 A. Place an anterior nasal pack
B. Consult interventional radiology for embolization of the bleeding vessel
C. Observe the patient for spontaneous resolution of bleeding
D. Administer andexanet alfa
E. Perform an endonasal examination, and apply topical silver nitrate
F. Perform nasal endoscopy and cauterize the bleeding vessel
G. Administer tranexamic acid intranasally
H. Reverse anticoagulation with fresh frozen plasma
I. Place an anterior and a posterior nasal pack
J. Perform surgical ligation of the sphenopalatine artery
